mcat_description.short: Pre-engineered steel buildings (PEB) are factory-fabricated, custom-designed structural steel building systems — comprising primary frames, secondary members, roofing, and cladding — supplied as a complete kit and bolted together on-site. Sold as turnkey supply-and-erect contracts or supply-only packages, typically quoted per sq ft of built-up area or per MT of steel.
mcat_description.long: A pre-engineered steel building is a complete structural system where all components — tapered primary portal frames (built-up welded I-sections), cold-formed secondary purlins and girts, profiled metal roofing and wall cladding, fasteners, and accessories — are designed, detailed, and fabricated in a controlled factory environment to project-specific dimensions, then transported and bolted together on-site. Design is governed by Indian Standards IS:800-2007 (general steel construction), IS:875 Parts 1–3 (dead, live, and wind loads), IS:1893 (seismic loads), and IS:2062 for structural steel grade, with some manufacturers also referencing AISC/MBMA for secondary members. The key structural innovation is variable-depth (tapered) members that optimise steel weight by matching section depth to the bending moment envelope, making PEB significantly lighter and faster to erect than conventional RCC or fabricated steel construction. In India, PEB is the dominant construction method for large-span industrial and logistics facilities, with the organised sector led by Kirby, Interarch, Pennar, Tata BlueScope, Zamil, and Everest Industries, alongside a large fragmented unorganised segment.

market_context: Pre-engineered steel buildings (PEB) are the dominant construction method for large-span industrial and logistics facilities in India, with the organised sector accounting for 35–40% of total market volume and six major players — Interarch, Kirby, Pennar, Phenix/M&B Engineering, Everest Industries, and Zamil — controlling 80–85% of the organised segment (single source — PA Wealth/Interarch analysis, low confidence on exact share figures). The unorganised segment (55–60% of total market) consists of smaller regional fabricators with lower capital investment, creating a highly fragmented competitive landscape. All PEB structures in India are designed to IS:800-2007 (general steel construction), IS:875 Parts 1–3 (dead, live, and wind loads), IS:1893 (seismic loads), and IS:2062 (structural steel grade); some manufacturers additionally reference AISC and MBMA for secondary cold-formed members. The market is driven by industrial capex growth, government infrastructure programmes (Atmanirbhar Bharat, PLI schemes), and the rapid expansion of e-commerce logistics and warehousing. Buyers in this category are primarily industrial developers, EPC contractors, and large manufacturers procuring complete turnkey solutions; the dominant buyer vocabulary uses 'PEB' as the standard abbreviation, with 'metal building' used interchangeably in some segments. Lead time from order to delivery is typically 8–12 weeks for standard projects.
